name: Interactive Paper Prototyping
phase: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that users can navigate our core onboarding flow without training. We will verify this by running 8 paper-prototype usability sessions, and consider it validated if ≥ 7 participants complete the primary conversion path without asking the facilitator for assistance.
schematic: Session at step 2 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Sketch screens, dropdowns and modals on index cards the facilitator can swap quickly.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Give one task; as the user taps paper, the facilitator plays the computer and lays the next state.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Note hesitation, mis-taps, spoken confusion and time to finish.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Sketch interface screens, dropdowns, and modals on separate paper index cards. Organize them systematically so a facilitator can swap them in and out quickly.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Give the user a clear task. As they touch the paper buttons with their finger, the facilitator acts as the computer, laying down the corresponding paper modal or screen state.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Note hesitation points, misplaced taps, verbalized confusion, and overall task completion times.

warning.label: Facilitator Coaxing
warning.text: Facilitators nod and coax through hesitations, hiding the flaw they were testing for.

warningFull: Facilitators often inadvertently guide participants through hesitation points with subtle body language, subconscious nods, or leading prompts, masking interface usability flaws.
